key_insight: Exciton–phonon linewidths stay sharp in polar semiconductors because center-of-mass recoil scattering is protected by electron–hole parity interference, which can completely suppress the 1s→1s channel in mass-symmetric materials.
engineering_relevance: For perovskite solar cells, exciton broadening cannot be predicted from the Fröhlich constant alone; designers must account for mass asymmetry, recoil momentum, and internal-state scattering channels when interpreting optical linewidths.
method: Restored exact exciton center-of-mass recoil in the exciton–phonon scattering model.
Derived a universal 1s→1s recoil channel at q* and an exact suppression law from hydrogenic Fröhlich theory.
Compared scattering strength across materials using the mass-asymmetry parameter η and the exciton Bohr scale q*aX.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative linewidth estimates: recoil remains active in GaAs (~2.2 meV) but is nearly absent in FAPbI3 (0.00 meV) and MAPbI3 (0.12 meV), far below the observed 27–40 meV perovskite linewidths.
watch_item: The recoil channel alone cannot explain the measured perovskite linewidths, so the model must include internal-state-changing and other inelastic processes to be predictive.
paper_title: Why polar excitons stay sharp: parity protection of the center-of-mass recoil channel in exciton-phonon scattering
